intro: Eerie minor-key keyboard line and sparse 808s; UGK's drawl arrives quickly.

title: Who Run It
intro: Dark descending synth bell figure, then Juicy J's shouted "Who run it?" — hugely recognizable from the beat-challenge era.

title: Cell Therapy
intro: Haunted music-box chimes and a creeping bassline — an unmistakable, instantly placeable Organized Noize intro.

title: Smile
intro: Mournful piano and 2Pac's spoken "you know what makes me unhappy" opening — distinctive from the first beat.

title: Snap Yo Fingers
intro: Sparse snapping percussion and Lil Jon's "Yeeeah!" ad-lib tag right at the top.

title: Ha
intro: Mannie Fresh's rubbery bounce beat with the signature clipped "ha" punctuation almost immediately.

title: Bling Bling
intro: Mannie Fresh keyboard glitter and the chanted "bling bling" hook — the song that gave the phrase to English.

title: Still Fly
intro: Bright plinking Mannie Fresh keys, then the sung "gator boots" hook; distinctive timbre from the first note.

title: Go DJ
intro: Mannie Fresh's marching snare and synth horn, with the "go DJ" chant arriving fast.

title: Lemonade
intro: Bouncy pitched vibraphone/marimba loop in a major key — a very identifiable Bangladesh beat.

title: You Know How We Do It
intro: Yes - warm smooth-funk guitar loop and synth pad; a well-known West Coast summer intro.

title: Runnin'
intro: Yes - the Stan Getz bossa-nova flute/bass sample (J Dilla production) is distinctive from the first beat.

title: Fantastic Voyage
intro: Yes - the Lakeside bassline and sung "Come along and ride" hook arrive very early.

title: 93 'Til Infinity
intro: Yes - the Billy Cobham jazz piano and soft upright bass loop is a famous cold open.

title: Bow Down
intro: Yes - the pounding kick with the chanted "Bow down" hook lands in the opening seconds.

title: The Bridge Is Over
intro: Lone hammered piano vamp with no drums — a very distinctive, instantly recognizable opening texture.

title: Hey Young World
intro: Soft chimes and the mellow Bob Marley-ish guitar loop, then Rick's "Hey young world" hook.

title: You Gots to Chill
intro: Zapp's "More Bounce to the Ounce" bassline and talkbox opening — very recognizable sample.

title: Smooth Operator
intro: Bouncy horn-and-bass loop with Kane's smooth opening line arriving quickly.

title: Say No Go
intro: Hall & Oates "I Can't Go for That" keyboard/drum loop up front, immediately familiar.

title: Daytona 500
intro: Bob James 'Nautilus' keyboard stabs — a sample most rap listeners know on contact

title: Who Got Da Props?
intro: Da Beatminerz dusty jazz-bass loop and Buckshot's nasal first bar

title: Grown Up
intro: Whistling, cartoonish keyboard loop opens cold; Danny's nasal delivery is unmistakable seconds in.

title: Really Doe
intro: Black Milk's eerie bell/chime loop and heavy kick open before Kendrick's hook.

title: Blockbuster Night Part 1
intro: Grinding industrial synth and thunderous drums slam in at zero seconds.

title: Rapp Snitch Knishes
intro: Dusty rock-guitar loop and hand-drum groove open; DOOM's baritone follows quickly.

title: Chum
intro: Lonely descending piano figure opens with no drums — sparse but very distinctive.

title: Venom
intro: Frantic staccato string ostinato opens cold — cinematic and immediately identifiable.

title: Introvert
intro: Big brass fanfare and timpani orchestral swell open before any rapping.

title: Front, Back & Side to Side
intro: Pimp C's woozy slow-rolling organ and clipped drums; the chopped-and-screwed-adjacent groove is distinctive but takes a few seconds.

title: Murder Was the Case
intro: Moderately - eerie minor-key synth and slow Death Row G-funk bass; recognizable to fans within a couple seconds.

title: This D.J.
intro: Moderately - lazy whistling G-funk synth lead over slow bass; a clear Warren G signature once a couple seconds play.

title: Throw Your Set in the Air
intro: Moderately - brassy horn stabs and Muggs' dusty drums; Cypress-identifiable by about two seconds.

title: Drop
intro: Moderately - Dilla's chopped, slightly off-kilter horn loop and crisp drums are a known backpack-era intro.

title: Tonite
intro: Moderately - bright Quik keyboard riff with live-feel bass and handclaps; a signature Compton funk opening.

title: New York, New York
intro: Moderately - Daz's ominous G-funk synth lead over heavy bass, with Snoop's hook close behind.

title: Same Song
intro: Moderately - P-Funk horn stabs and bouncy bass; the first notes are clearly Digital Underground.

title: Real Muthaphuckkin G's
intro: Yes - the whistling high synth and Eazy's laugh/ad-libs make the first seconds very distinctive.

title: Streiht Up Menace
intro: Moderately - slow ominous synth line and heavy kick from the Menace II Society soundtrack; distinctive mood at once.

title: Paparazzi
intro: Moderately - haunting flute/synth loop with knocking drums before the first bar; memorable opening.

title: Afro Puffs
intro: Moderately - Dre/Daz funk bass and squelchy synth with Rage's hard first bar arriving early.

title: Vica Versa
intro: Aggressive marching snare and ominous synth with Troy's shouted ad-libs; recognizable to Southern rap fans within a couple seconds.

title: Born and Raised in Compton
intro: Partly - talkbox-flavored synth and slow funk drums; fans place it quickly, casuals need more seconds.

title: Let's Play House
intro: Partly - squealing high synth and Death Row bass bounce; recognizable to West Coast listeners.
